packages.the client package contains: the kscope command and the launcher that picks your platform's binary
packages.the platform package contains: one program, the memory engine, as proprietary object code. The setup work that kscope init performs is compiled into that same program, so there is no second executable to install.
packages.there are no account or sign-in commands: Signing in, linking an account, listing devices and revoking a session are verbs of a second program, which is not published on any channel. Nothing you can install carries them. A key is all Kaleidoscope asks for, and your vault has never depended on an account.
packages.there is no Python package: kscope-memory is registered on PyPI, but only as a 0.0.0 placeholder that ships no working code; its own summary says it is not yet released. kaleidoscope-memory was planned and never registered.

summary: Kaleidoscope is installable from npm and needs a key to run. Nothing is signed for release, and there is no account to sign in to.
the platform matrix: Which machines a program is built and published for, which have been run on, and which have only had a compiler check is stated once, at /platform-support.json. What this record carries about platforms is the package inventory below — which platform packages exist — and not the build, run or compiler-check status of any of them.
what you can do today: Run it with a key, which we send by email on request.
Give a project a memory with kscope init, and connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode to it.
Read the documentation, the command reference and the two-tool agent contract.
what you cannot do today: Run it on Windows: creating a vault there is refused until the filesystem work lands.
Run it without a key: email contact@kleosresearch.xyz and we will send you one.

Run kscope connect, kscope disconnect, kscope config, kscope doctor or kscope profile use: those verbs belong to a second program that is not published on any channel. What ships is kscope, and kscope init does the setup.
Install a Python package: kscope-memory on PyPI is a 0.0.0 placeholder with no working code in it, and kaleidoscope-memory was never registered.
Verify a signature: nothing is signed for release.
Use hosted memory: there is no service, endpoint, API or waitlist.
Reproduce our benchmark results: the full method is not published yet.
Rely on any support commitment: none is offered.
